The proposed answer of 36 is incorrect. The correct perimeter is 42 inches.

The error is the claim that each triangle's side equals one-sixth of the hexagon's perimeter. In the division, each triangle has two sides that are radii of the hexagon and one side that is a hexagon side. All three sides of each equilateral triangle are equal, so each triangle's side equals the hexagon's side length, not a sixth of its perimeter.

1. The triangle's perimeter is 21 inches, so each side is 21 / 3 = 7 inches.
2. The hexagon's side length equals the triangle's side length, so it is 7 inches.
3. The hexagon has 6 equal sides, so its perimeter is 6 × 7 = 42 inches.

The proposed proportion 21/3 = x/6 has no valid basis, and the arithmetic that follows (18 = x/2) doesn't follow from it either.

VERDICT: REJECT
